assessment.overall_rationale: This is a near-identical baseline replicate: the cilia biogenesis module (L1/R1), endothelial cilia mechanosensing module (L2/R2), and Wnt/Fzd4-Gata2-Eng regulator module (L3/R3) each match one-to-one with near-perfect similarity, while cross-pairs share genes/tissue context but diverge in core mechanism (structural biogenesis vs. mechanosensory function vs. transcriptional regulation), warranting low partial-overlap or context-only scores.

pair_scores.rationale: Both describe the identical cilia biogenesis machinery (BBSome, IFT, transition zone, distal appendages) with essentially the same gene set and mechanistic framing.
Shares the same cilia gene set with right module 2 but frames them as flow-mechanosensing output rather than structural biogenesis, a different core mechanism emphasis.
Cilia structural genes versus Wnt/TGF-b endothelial transcriptional regulators share only the brain vascular tissue context, not mechanism.
Left module 2 frames the same ciliary genes as mechanosensors for blood flow while right module 1 frames them as biogenesis machinery, overlapping genes but different central mechanism/output.
Both describe endothelial primary cilia as flow-shear mechanosensors driving postnatal BBB maturation using the same gene set and evidence (KLF2, shear response).
Ciliary mechanosensation and transcriptional/receptor regulators of endothelial identity share only the endothelial/BBB context, not mechanism or gene roles.
Regulatory Wnt/TGF-b transcription factors versus structural cilia biogenesis genes share no mechanistic overlap beyond the same overall program.
Endothelial identity/BBB transcriptional regulators differ mechanistically from ciliary mechanosensation, overlapping only in the shared endothelial/BBB context.
Both describe the same Fzd4/Gata2/Eng regulator trio governing Norrin-Wnt CNS vascular identity and BBB integrity, differing only in that left retains Tet1 as a supporting gene.
